Why Local Data Matters More Than Another Net-Zero Policy

A target at group level becomes useful when site teams can see the choices it asks them to make.

Pupsi Phull · Phull Insights22 September 20262 min readSustainable Performance
Evidence boundary

Personal analysis and professional reflection based on earlier postgraduate work. Named-company examples describe historical research, not current 2026 corporate policies, figures or commitments. No unpublished case result is represented as a verified outcome.

Why this matters

Corporate targets can be clear while the daily decisions that support them remain invisible to local teams.

What the evidence suggests

The historical DHL-related concept behind this article explored a local data application. Its value was not the app itself, but the possibility of connecting site-level activity, ownership and feedback to a broader sustainability ambition.

What it looks like in practice

A useful local view should show data provenance and uncertainty. It should help a manager distinguish a change in activity from a change in environmental performance, then decide what to test next.

Practical next steps

Three things leaders can do now

01

Identify the environmental decision a site manager can actually influence.

02

Check whether the local data is complete and comparable before setting a target.

03

Make the next action and its owner visible in the same review as the measure.

Phull Insights Perspective

The view beneath the headline.

Better reporting is not the end point. The value appears when evidence changes an operating choice and the result is checked.
